correctness.rationale: Exact prescribed-edge moments give a scalar covariance on the zero-vertex-degree coefficient subspace; direct two-cut overlap yields the stated circulant kernel; root-of-unity identity gives all eigenvalues. Graph Laplacian and constant projector invert the spectrum. Positive polynomial derivatives and monotonicity of t sin(pi/t) rigorously establish the m=5 mode switch and every exact condition ratio, with limit 1/6. Standalone standard-library checker exhausts m=2..7, verifies inverse at m=2..17, extrema at m=2..499; finite checks corroborate but are not used as infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Inspected primary 2021 random-chord study and complete scientific public texts of nearest pairing-cut, chord-length covariance, and complete-graph matching-scheme findings. Those different observations do not state or directly dominate the evaluated rotating-semicircle cyclic Green, local-plus-rank-one precision, unique m=5 extremum switch and sharp 1/6 coefficient. Standard pairing probabilities and Fourier identities are explicitly credited. Historical coverage by a more general cut-process formula remains a residual priority risk.
residual_risks: A general fixed-size perfect-matching association-scheme covariance could already imply the scalar edge-coefficient lemma; the evaluated contribution depends on the specialized cyclic inversion and all-size spectral extrema.
An uninspected earlier work on rotating half-circle chord flux or a Green kernel from matching cut profiles could subsume the specialized result.
The Acan paper was not inspected in entire original full text; only publicly accessible article introduction and abstract were read.
Semantic searches and current claims cannot prove global priority.

value.rationale: Equal-half crossing counts form a canonical angle-resolved tomography of circular random matchings. The theorem identifies all linear observational redundancies, proves an explicit local precision operator with a rank-one conservation correction, detects a unique finite-size transition in most observable modes at m=5 and calculates the sharp quadratic-scale condition constant 1/6. These are natural structural and stability invariants beyond a routine moment estimate or arbitrary finite table.
